name: GALE CRATER — lower Mount Sharp
blurb: Curiosity's ground, read from the 1 m/px HiRISE mosaic — the finest DEM of anywhere on Mars, and the only site here whose landforms are resolved at the scale a robot walks.

meta.site: Gale Crater — lower Mount Sharp flank
meta.citation: USGS Astrogeology / MSL — HiRISE DEM mosaic of Gale Crater, 1 m/px, v3
meta.grid: azimuthal equidistant about the site, resampled bilinear
meta.resolution_note: source product is 1 m/px; this 512px grid at 0.25 m/px spans 128.0 source posts and is a 4x bilinear resampling of them — interpolation, not added detail
meta.note: Rocky uphill traction. 1 m/px HiRISE, the finest Mars DEM there is.

lope.label: LOPE
lope.blurb: The gait the Apollo crews adopted within minutes on every mission. One foot at a time, airborne between every step — a walk whose double support has been replaced by flight.

bound.label: BOUND
bound.blurb: Both feet together, everything into the vertical. The robot is identical on all three bodies and pushes identically, so the whole difference in height and hang is the field.

trip.label: TRIP + RECOVER
trip.blurb: A caught toe, and the fall that follows. Toppling is a pendulum about the toe, so the time to go over scales as 1/sqrt(g): 0.93 s on Earth against 2.28 s on the Moon. That extra second and a third is what the Apollo crews used to get a hand down.
